1.title: Encryption and Masking
1.text: Welcome to Module sixteen: Encryption and Masking. This module covers the task statement: ensure data encryption and masking. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Mask and anonymize data according to compliance laws or company policy. Use encryption keys (A W S K M S (Key Management Service)) to encrypt and decrypt data. Configure encryption across A W S account boundaries. Enable encryption in transit or before transit. --.

1.title: Case Check-In: Kestrel Freight Protects Customer Data
1.text: Our running case is Kestrel Freight. Kestrel Freight Protects Customer Data. Test teams need realistic data but not real names and phone numbers. Analysts need trends by customer, but not who the customer is. A privacy law limits how personal data may be stored and shared. Your job: keep the value of the data and remove the risk.

1.title: Masking and Anonymization
1.text: Masking and Anonymization. Masking (static). What it does: Replaces values with fake or partial ones (-one thousand two hundred thirty-four) in a copy. Reversible?: No. Use it for: Test and development data. Dynamic masking. What it does: Hides or partly shows values at query time by role; stored data unchanged. Reversible?: Yes (for authorized roles). Use it for: Redshift dynamic data masking. Redaction. What it does: Removes the value. Reversible?: No. Use it for: Free text, logs. Hashing. What it does: One-way fingerprint of a value; the same input gives the same hash. Reversible?: No. Use it for: Joining on a masked key, matching without revealing.

1.title: Masking and Anonymization, continued
1.text: Masking and Anonymization, continued. Tokenization. What it does: Replaces the value with a token; the real value lives in a secure vault. Reversible?: Yes, with the vault. Use it for: Payment data, I Ds. Pseudonymization. What it does: Replaces identifiers with a pseudonym; a key or table can re-identify. Reversible?: Yes. Use it for: Analytics that must link records. Anonymization. What it does: Irreversibly removes the link to a person (generalize, aggregate, suppress, add noise). Reversible?: No. Use it for: Sharing data publicly; data that falls outside privacy law when truly anonymous. Generalization. What it does: Reduce precision (age thirty-four to thirty to thirty-nine, full address to region). Reversible?: No. Use it for: Statistics.

1.title: Masking and Anonymization, continued
1.text: Masking and Anonymization, continued. Pseudonymized data is still personal data under many laws (for example the G D P R (General Data Protection Regulation)) because it can be re-identified; truly anonymized data is not. Choose by need: analysis needs joins to hash or pseudonym; testing to static mask; role-based viewing to dynamic masking or column permissions; sharing externally to anonymize.

1.title: AWS tools
1.text: A W S tools. Find personal data. Amazon Macie (S three), Glue detect-P I I (personally identifiable information) transform, Amazon Comprehend (text). Mask or hash columns in a pipeline. A W S Glue DataBrew (mask, hash, encrypt, shuffle, substitute), A W S Glue E T L (extract, transform, load) (P I I detection and redaction), Lambda. Show masked values to some users. Redshift dynamic data masking, Lake Formation column and row filters (Module fifteen), views. Protect model prompts and outputs. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails (filters sensitive information). Exam tip: "Give developers realistic test data with no real personal data" to mask or substitute in a copy (DataBrew or Glue). "Show the last four digits to support staff only" to dynamic data masking.

1.title: Encryption Keys with AWS KMS
1.text: Encryption Keys with A W S K M S. The figure shows this: Envelope encryption: a data key encrypts the data, and a K M S key encrypts the data key; the encrypted data key is stored with the data and only K M S can decrypt it. A W S Key Management Service (K M S) creates and controls encryption keys; keys never leave K M S unencrypted; every use is logged in CloudTrail. Key types.

1.title: Encryption Keys with AWS KMS, continued
1.text: Encryption Keys with A W S K M S, continued. A W S owned key. Who manages: A W S (not visible). Notes: Free; no control or audit. A W S managed key (aws or S three, aws or redshift...). Who manages: A W S for your account. Notes: Rotated every year; fixed key policy. Customer managed key (C M K). Who manages: You. Notes: Your key policy, rotation choice, can be used across accounts, can be disabled or scheduled for deletion; charged per key. Symmetric keys (one key to encrypt and decrypt, default) and asymmetric keys (public and private pair: signing and encryption outside A W S).

1.title: Encryption Keys with AWS KMS, continued
1.text: Encryption Keys with A W S K M S, continued. Envelope encryption: K M S encrypts only small data keys (GenerateDataKey); the data key encrypts the large data; this is how S three, E B S (Elastic Block Store), Redshift and others use K M S. Access control: the key policy is the primary control (I A M policies work only if the key policy allows I A M (Identity and Access Management)); grants give temporary, specific permission to A W S services; permissions are separate for kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey. Rotation: for customer managed keys, automatic rotation (every three hundred sixty-five days by default, with a custom period option, plus on-demand rotation) keeps the same key I D; old key material is kept so old data stays readable.

1.title: Encryption Keys with AWS KMS, continued
1.text: Encryption Keys with A W S K M S, continued. Deletion: a waiting period of seven to thirty days before a key is deleted; data encrypted under a deleted key is unrecoverable.

1.title: Encryption at rest in the data services
1.text: Encryption at rest in the data services. Amazon S three. S S E (server-side encryption)-S three on every new object by default; S S E-K M S (your key, audit trail; bucket keys cut K M S request cost); D S S E (dual-layer server-side encryption)-K M S (two layers); S S E-C (your key, supplied per request; disabled by default on new buckets ); client-side. Amazon Redshift. K M S-encrypted clusters and snapshots (Redshift Serverless is always encrypted). Amazon R D S (Relational Database Service) or Aurora. K M S, chosen at creation (to encrypt an unencrypted database, copy a snapshot with encryption and restore). Amazon DynamoDB. Always encrypted at rest; choose A W S owned, A W S managed or customer managed key. A W S Glue. Security configurations encrypt S three targets, CloudWatch logs and job bookmarks.

1.title: Encryption at rest in the data services, continued
1.text: Encryption at rest in the data services, continued. Kinesis Data Streams or Firehose. Server-side encryption with K M S. Amazon E M R (Elastic MapReduce). Security configuration: at-rest (S three E M R F S (E M R File System), local disks, E B S) and in-transit options. Athena. Encrypt query results in S three per workgroup. Amazon E B S or E F S (Elastic File System). K M S. Exam tip: "Control the key, audit every use, and be able to disable access quickly" to S S E-K M S with a customer managed key. "Cut the K M S request cost of an S three-heavy pipeline" to S three Bucket Keys.

2.title: Encryption across Account Boundaries
2.text: Encryption across Account Boundaries. The figure shows this: Cross-account encryption needs permission on both sides: the key policy in the owner account must allow the other account, and an I A M policy in the other account must allow its role to use the key. Two permissions are needed: the key policy (in the key's account) must allow the other account (or role), and an I A M policy in the other account must allow its role to use that key.

2.title: Encryption across Account Boundaries, continued
2.text: Encryption across Account Boundaries, continued. Use a customer managed key for anything shared: A W S managed keys and A W S owned keys cannot be shared with another account.

2.title: Encryption across Account Boundaries, continued
2.text: Encryption across Account Boundaries, continued. Typical cases:; S three objects encrypted with S S E-K M S read by another account: bucket policy (or access point) allows the principal and the key policy allows kms:Decrypt; Sharing an encrypted R D S or Redshift snapshot: encrypt with a customer managed key, share the snapshot, and share the key with the other account; the recipient copies the snapshot and re-encrypts with its own key; Lake Formation or Redshift data sharing across accounts: grant on the data and allow the key; Replication to another account or Region: allow K M S on both keys.

2.title: Encryption across Account Boundaries, continued
2.text: Encryption across Account Boundaries, continued. Grants and conditions: use kms:ViaService (only through S three), encryption context, and organization conditions to limit use. Exam tip: "Another account cannot read objects in a shared bucket that use S S E-K M S" to add the account to the C M K (customer managed key)'s key policy and kms:Decrypt to its role; an A W S managed key cannot be shared.

2.title: Encryption in Transit or Before Transit
2.text: Encryption in Transit or Before Transit. The figure shows this: Protecting data in motion: T L S to the service, private network paths, and client-side encryption before the data leaves the source so only ciphertext travels. In transit equals while moving: use T L S (H T T P S); A W S service A P I s use T L S; enforce it:; S three: a bucket policy that denies requests when the secure transport condition is false (and can require a minimum T L S version); Redshift: set require ssl in the parameter group; R D S or Aurora: require S S L (for example rds.force ssl for PostgreSQL); Kafka (M S K) and Kinesis: T L S in transit; E M R: in-transit encryption options; A P I Gateway and load balancers: H T T P S with A C M (A W S Certificate Manager) certificates.

2.title: Encryption in Transit or Before Transit, continued
2.text: Encryption in Transit or Before Transit, continued. Private paths reduce exposure: V P C (Virtual Private Cloud) endpoints and PrivateLink, Site-to-Site V P N (virtual private network) (IPsec), Direct Connect (private, encrypt with V P N or MACsec if required). Before transit (client-side encryption): encrypt on the source before sending, so only ciphertext travels and is stored; the service never sees plaintext: A W S Encryption S D K (software development kit), S three encryption client, DynamoDB encryption client; keys come from K M S (GenerateDataKey). Choose: T L S is the baseline; client-side encryption for the highest control (A W S cannot read the data) at the cost of key handling and less service-side processing (the service cannot query encrypted values). Exam tip: "Make sure no one can upload or read over H T T P" to bucket policy denying the secure transport condition equals false. "A W S must never see plaintext" to client-side encryption.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Masking techniques: Static mask (copy), dynamic mask (query time, by role), redact, hash (one-way), tokenize (vault), pseudonymize (reversible. Tools: Macie or Glue detect-P I I or Comprehend to find; DataBrew or Glue to mask. K M S keys: A W S owned, A W S managed (yearly rotation, fixed policy), customer managed (your policy, rotation, shareable, seven to thirty day deletion wait). K M S access: Key policy first; I A M works only if the key policy allows it; grants for services; kms:Encrypt or Decrypt or GenerateDataKey. At rest: S three S S E-S three default, S S E-K M S ( plus bucket keys), D S S E-K M S, S S E-C. Cross-account: Customer managed key; key policy plus I A M policy; A W S managed keys cannot be shared. In transit: T L S everywhere; the secure transport condition, Redshift require ssl, R D S force S S L; V P C endpoints or V P N or Direct Connect ( plus MACsec).

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Kestrel Freight's developers need realistic test data without any real customer names or phone numbers. What is the best approach? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. Static masking or substitution in a copy keeps realistic structure while removing personal data. Encryption does not remove personal data from authorized readers.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Select two. An S three bucket in account A holds objects encrypted with S S E-K M S under a customer managed key. A role in account B cannot read them even though the bucket policy allows it. Which two actions fix this? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and E. Cross-account K M S use needs permission in the key policy and in the caller's I A M policy. A W S managed keys cannot be shared.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A team must ensure that no client can send or retrieve S three data over unencrypted connections. What should be configured? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. The the secure transport condition condition identifies requests made over H T T P, which the policy denies.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all three answers. Question one: D. Question two: A and E. Question three: A. In the next module, we continue the course.
